title.rendered: Doble’s Independent Drivers’ success recognised at TOCA Awards

excerpt.rendered: Twelve months after missing out on the Independent Drivers’ Championship...

content.rendered:
Twelve months after missing out on the Independent Drivers’ Championship by just four points, Mikey Doble was among those taking centre stage at the 2026 TOCA Awards, collecting his trophy following a remarkable campaign in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

The LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver finally lifted the crown that had eluded him in the previous two seasons, adding to his 2024 Jack Sears Trophy success and becoming a two-time BTCC title winner.

Returning with new Audi A3 Saloon machinery for 2026, the 27-year-old immediately demonstrated his intentions with an outright victory in the opening race at Donington Park, giving Power Maxed Racing's latest challenger a winning debut.

That success proved to be the first of many highlights for the Surrey racer, who went on to register seven Independent victories, eight further top-three finishes in the class and a second outright triumph at Croft.

Despite his strong form, Doble faced stiff competition throughout the year, with Gordon Shedden, Charles Rainford and Daryl De Leon all mounting challenges for the Independent Drivers’ crown.

Indeed, consistency proved just as important as outright speed, with Doble holding a slender five-point advantage over De Leon at the summer break before strengthening his position during the second half of the season.

His commanding lights-to-flag victory at Croft proved to be a defining moment, while further success followed at Silverstone, where Doble celebrated his maiden Qualifying Race win and pole position before adding another overall top-three finish on Sunday.

Heading into the final weekend at Brands Hatch with a 25-point advantage over Shedden, Doble held his nerve to wrap up the championship with a race to spare, producing an impressive drive to fourth overall in the second contest and recording his seventh Independent victory of the year.

The Audi racer ultimately finished the season with 421 points, 39 clear of teammate Aiden Moffat, who completed a one-two finish for Power Maxed Racing in the Independent Drivers’ standings.

Doble also took sixth place in the overall Drivers’ Championship, achieving his pre-season ambition of becoming a multiple race winner, finishing inside the top six and lifting the Independent Drivers’ title.

His performances also helped LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing to the Independent Teams’ Championship, completing a memorable year for the squad and its new Audi machinery.

title.rendered: Patterson's breakthrough season earns Jack Sears Trophy honours

excerpt.rendered: Sixteen Jack Sears Trophy victories, a maiden championship crown and...

content.rendered:
Sixteen Jack Sears Trophy victories, a maiden championship crown and a first outright BTCC podium made 2026 a breakthrough season for Dexter Patterson, whose achievements were recognised at the annual TOCA Awards at Silverstone on Saturday evening (7 November).

The Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing driver enjoyed his most successful BTCC season to date, wrapping up the Jack Sears Trophy title with an event to spare before ending the year on a high at Brands Hatch.

Having joined Power Maxed Racing for 2026, Patterson quickly adapted to the team's new Audi A3 Saloon machinery, making an immediate impression with a clean sweep of Jack Sears Trophy victories at the opening event at Donington Park.

Two seventh-place finishes and a sixth overall marked his strongest BTCC weekend to date, providing an early indication of the progress he would make throughout the season.

Despite his impressive start, the championship battle was far from straightforward, with Restart Racing newcomer James Dorlin emerging as his closest challenger during the first half of the year.

Dorlin overturned Patterson's early advantage at Brands Hatch Indy and remained a strong contender through Snetterton, before the Scottish racer responded with another three Jack Sears Trophy victories at Oulton Park to reclaim the championship lead heading into the summer break.

With just two points separating the pair following the next meeting at Thruxton, Patterson produced one of his standout performances of the season on home soil at Knockhill.

Three further class victories, alongside an impressive fourth-place finish in the final race, saw him regain control of the championship and establish a 17-point advantage at the top of the standings.

The momentum continued on Donington Park's Grand Prix layout, where another clean sweep extended his lead to 77 points, putting him firmly in command of the title battle heading into the closing stages of the season.

Patterson's consistency ultimately proved decisive at Silverstone, where his advantage became mathematically unassailable in Sunday's opening race, confirming him as Jack Sears Trophy champion.

Already assured of his first BTCC championship title, the Audi driver arrived at Brands Hatch for the season finale with an opportunity to add another significant achievement to his growing list of successes.

Starting the final race from reverse-grid pole position, Patterson battled among the outright frontrunners throughout the contest before a post-race penalty for Ricky Collard promoted him to third, earning him his maiden overall BTCC podium.

title.rendered: Sam Osborne: Looking back on eight seasons in the BTCC

excerpt.rendered: From his first podium at Donington Park to an emotional...

content.rendered:
From his first podium at Donington Park to an emotional maiden victory at Silverstone, Sam Osborne enjoyed plenty of memorable moments during his eight seasons in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

The NAPA Racing UK driver brought his BTCC career to a close at Brands Hatch last month, having established himself as a familiar face on the grid since making his debut with EXCELR8 Motorsport in 2019.

After graduating from the MINI CHALLENGE and Renault UK Clio Cup, Osborne made his championship bow at Brands Hatch Indy behind the wheel of the MG6 GT.

His first championship points followed at Snetterton later that season, before a switch to MB Motorsport's Honda Civic Type R in 2020 delivered his first two top-ten finishes, including an impressive seventh place at Donington Park.

The #77 then joined the Motorbase Performance operation in 2021, beginning a six-season association with the Ford squad, after it later became NAPA Racing UK. After finishing fourth in the Jack Sears Trophy standings in 2022, a move into NAPA Racing UK's expanded four-car line-up brought another milestone.

Osborne secured his maiden overall podium in the rain-affected second race of the 2023 season opener at Donington Park, finishing third. His performances continued to improve, culminating in a career-best 15th in the Drivers' Championship in 2024, when he finished eight of the final nine races inside the top ten.

That impressive run also helped the Nottinghamshire racer secure the runner-up spot in the Jack Sears Trophy, having dramatically reduced the deficit to eventual champion Mikey Doble during the second half of the campaign.

The standout moment, however, came at Silverstone in September 2025. Starting the reverse-grid contest from pole position, Osborne delivered a determined defensive drive to keep Josh Cook at bay and secure his first BTCC victory on his 202nd start.

The emotional celebrations with his father, Pete Osborne, and the NAPA Racing UK squad provided one of the most memorable scenes of the season, bringing a long-awaited reward for his years of hard work.

Returning for one final campaign in 2026, Osborne added third place in the Jack Sears Trophy standings to his career achievements, before bringing his 224-race BTCC journey to a close during a memorable weekend of celebrations at Brands Hatch, where NAPA Racing UK secured both the Teams' and Manufacturers'/Constructors' titles.

title.rendered: LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing celebrates Independent Teams' triumph

excerpt.rendered: LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing celebrated its...

content.rendered:
LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing celebrated its 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship success at the TOCA Awards on Saturday evening (7 November), collecting the Independent Teams' Championship trophy following an impressive campaign.

The Silverstone ceremony marked another significant achievement for Power Maxed Racing, which claimed its second Independent Teams' crown in three seasons after a memorable year with its new Audi A3 Saloons.

With Mikey Doble and Aiden Moffat spearheading the LKQ Euro Car Parts-backed entry, the team made an immediate impression when Doble claimed an outright victory in the opening race at Donington Park, giving the new Audi a winning debut.

That success set the tone for a campaign in which the pair combined for 13 Independent race victories, helping the squad lead the championship standings from the opening weekend through to the season finale.

Despite its strong start, however, the title was far from guaranteed. WSR and Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport both mounted challenges throughout the year, with the former closing to within a single point of the leaders at Oulton Park heading into the summer break.

Power Maxed Racing responded impressively during the second half of the campaign, gradually rebuilding its advantage through consistent points finishes and further class victories.

Among the standout moments was Doble's second outright win of the season at Croft, while the penultimate meeting at Silverstone delivered arguably the team's greatest achievement of the year.

Moffat led Doble home in the opening race to secure Power Maxed Racing's first-ever BTCC one-two finish, having already completed a one-two in the previous day's Qualifying Race. Moffat added another overall top-three finish in the final encounter, helping the team establish a 33-point championship advantage heading into Brands Hatch.

The title was ultimately secured with a race to spare on the Grand Prix circuit, as Doble claimed another Independent victory in the second contest to confirm both his maiden Independent Drivers' crown and the Teams' title.

By the conclusion of the campaign, LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing had amassed 515 points, finishing 46 clear of nearest challenger WSR, while also finishing third in the overall Teams' Championship.

With Doble also crowned Independent Drivers' Champion and Moffat taking the runner-up position, the team's achievements were deservedly recognised at the TOCA Awards, bringing a memorable 2026 campaign to a fitting conclusion.

title.rendered: Double MINI CHALLENGE JCW Champion Tom Ovenden Makes BTCC move with Team VERTU

excerpt.rendered: Double MINI CHALLENGE JCW champion Tom Ovenden will make the...

content.rendered:
Double MINI CHALLENGE JCW champion Tom Ovenden will make the move up into the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship next season after signing a deal to make his series debut with Team VERTU.

Ovenden, who successfully defended the JCW title this season, will join forces with former champion Tom Ingram in the second Hyundai i30 Fastback N running in the colours of Vertu, Britain’s fourth-largest automotive group.

Fellow debutant Noah Young and a fourth driver still to be confirmed will complete the four-strong line-up when the season gets underway at Donington Park in April.

Ovenden’s move into a race seat in Britain’s premier racing series marks the latest phase of a hugely impressive career that started on two wheels in motocross before he followed in the footsteps of father Tristan by taking up rallycross.

Having clinched the British Junior Rallycross Championship title in 2020, Ovenden moved into circuit racing in the MINI CHALLENGE Trophy the following year with EXCELR8, going on to lift the championship crown in 2023 before moving into the headline JCW class.

Becoming the first driver to win both the Trophy and JCW titles in 2025, Ovenden then defended his crown in dramatic fashion this year, winning the title by a single point at Brands Hatch.

Alongside his role in the MINI CHALLENGE, Ovenden has spent recent seasons as part of EXCELR8’s Young Driver Programme and was official reserve and development driver for Team VERTU during 2026.

Having already had the opportunity to sample the Hyundai in the past through that role, Ovenden will embark on a pre-season testing programme in the New Year in preparation for his touring car debut.

Tom Ovenden said: “I feel very lucky and very privileged to be making the move into the BTCC for 2027, and this really is one of those dream come true moments.

“It’s an unbelievable opportunity for me, and is all the more special because of the fact that I’m joining the grid with the same team that I’ve been part of since I was 16 and took my first steps into circuit racing.

“When I joined EXCELR8 in the MINI Cooper, my goal was always to get to touring cars but I never imagined that things would go the way they have done. Winning three titles during my time in the MINI CHALLENGE has been amazing and it’s mental to think that I’m going to be a BTCC driver!

“I have to say a huge thank you to EXCELR8 and Vertu for putting their faith in me because there is no other team I’d want to do this with. I know and trust EXCELR8 and the people in the team, and in Tom Ingram, I have the perfect team-mate to learn from during my rookie season.

“I have no idea what to expect when it comes to results, but I know I’m going to have a good car underneath me and one of the best teams behind me. The Jack Sears Trophy will be an obvious aim, and if I could push for a podium finish then it would be amazing.”

Justina Williams, EXCELR8 Team Owner said: “Tom has developed a huge amount as a driver from the moment he joined us as a 16-year-old making his circuit racing debut, as his record in recent seasons has shown.

“To win multiple titles in such a competitive one-make series is no mean feat, and he has worked really hard both on and off the circuit to earn the opportunity to move into a touring car seat.

“I have every confidence in him going into 2027, and we are all excited to see what he can achieve as a BTCC driver.”

title.rendered: Tom Chilton: Looking back on 20 seasons in the BTCC

excerpt.rendered: Few drivers have enjoyed a career quite like Tom Chilton,...

content.rendered:
Few drivers have enjoyed a career quite like Tom Chilton, whose 20 seasons in the British Touring Car Championship included 19 victories, an Independents' title and a host of memorable moments across more than two decades.

The Surrey racer brought his BTCC journey to a close at Brands Hatch last month, returning to the very circuit where his remarkable career began as a 17-year-old in 2002.

Driving a Barwell Motorsport-run Vauxhall Astra Coupé, Chilton became the youngest driver ever to compete in the championship at the time, making an immediate impression with third place in his debut race weekend on the Grand Prix layout. Remarkably, the teenager had never driven the circuit before and had walked the track the previous evening to familiarise himself with its challenges.

That opening podium set the tone for an impressive early career, with a move to Arena Motorsport's Honda operation bringing his maiden victory at Silverstone in 2004. At just 19 years of age, Chilton became the youngest race winner in BTCC history, a record that still stands today.

Four further victories followed in 2005, helping the youngster secure fifth in the Drivers' Championship despite missing several races, before spells with VX Racing and Team Halfords added more silverware.

Reuniting with Arena Motorsport in 2009, Chilton enjoyed another successful chapter behind the wheel of the Ford Focus ST. Three race wins and four pole positions in 2010 helped the Brit claim the Independents Drivers' title, while two further victories followed in 2011.

A move to the FIA World Touring Car Championship then saw Chilton compete internationally, recording seven victories and finishing third overall in 2017, when he also secured the Independents' Trophy.

His BTCC return with Power Maxed Racing that same year was followed by a switch to Motorbase Performance in 2018, where a consistent campaign delivered a career-best third in the overall Drivers' Championship.

Further success came with EXCELR8 Motorsport, which he joined in 2022. A perfectly timed switch to wet tyres earned Chilton victory in a dramatic race at Donington Park in 2023, while the #3 Hyundai racer enjoyed a particularly strong 2025 campaign, collecting two victories and six podium finishes.

There was still time for one final triumph in 2026, as Chilton dominated the reverse-grid contest at Knockhill to claim his 19th BTCC victory, and third in Scotland.

His final appearance at Brands Hatch brought the story full circle, with the 41-year-old signing off at the scene of his maiden podium, surrounded by family, friends and supporters after a remarkable career spanning 24 years.

title.rendered: TOCA Awards celebrate 2026 success stories

excerpt.rendered: The stars of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship...

content.rendered:
The stars of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship and its support series came together at Silverstone on Saturday evening for the annual TOCA Awards.

The event celebrated the champions and standout performers who made the 2026 season such a memorable one, bringing the curtain down on another year of competition across the TOCA package.

Ash Sutton was honoured for securing a record-breaking fifth BTCC Drivers’ Championship, while Alliance Racing/Ford was crowned Manufacturers’/Constructors’ Champion and NAPA Racing UK collected the Teams’ title.

Mikey Doble received the Independent Drivers’ award, with LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing taking the Independent Teams’ crown, whilst Dexter Patterson was also recognised for winning the Jack Sears Trophy.

The support-series champions were celebrated too, including Dries Van Langendonck claiming the Wera Tools F4 British Championship title, Tom Ovenden retaining the Power Maxed MINI CHALLENGE JCW crown, and Callum Voisin winning the Porsche Carwow Carrera Cup Great Britain.

Alongside the championship trophies, the evening recognised achievements beyond the final standings, with a number of Special Awards also being celebrated.

Over the coming weeks, we’ll look back in more detail at the champions and award winners, exploring the stories behind their achievements and the moments that defined their 2026 campaigns.

title.rendered: Format changes for 2027 BTCC

excerpt.rendered: Following the annual end-of-season meeting between TOCA, the BTCC Series...

content.rendered:
Following the annual end-of-season meeting between TOCA, the BTCC Series Organiser, and the teams, a revised race weekend format has been agreed for the 2027 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

Practice Sessions

Saturday will begin with two 25-minute practice sessions.

These replace the single sessions used in 2026, giving teams and drivers two separate sessions to prepare for Qualifying.

Qualifying

A single 20-minute Qualifying session, with all cars running in one group, will set the grid for the Qualifying Race. Teams will be able to run with the minimum fuel needed for the session.

In 2026, the field was split into two groups, each with a 15-minute session, and cars were under parc fermé conditions from the start of Qualifying until after the Qualifying Race.

Qualifying Race

The Qualifying Race, known as the ‘Race to Pole’, will run over approximately half the distance of a standard BTCC race. A longer break will take place between qualifying and the ‘Race to Pole’, giving teams more time between sessions.

In 2026, the pit lane opened for the Qualifying Race 15 minutes after the second qualifying group finished.

Reverse Grid Draw

The reverse-grid draw for Sunday’s final race will cover drivers who finish tenth to 16th in race two.

The 2026 draw covered drivers who finished sixth to 12th.

Friday Shakedowns

Friday shakedowns will return at selected events, giving teams the option to run ahead of Saturday practice.

In recent seasons, all shakedowns took place earlier in the week outside of the circuit venues - at a time and location of each team’s choosing.

TOCA is finalising further changes, including revisions to the boost regulations, and will confirm the details in due course.

title.rendered: Tom Ingram extends Team VERTU stay with new multi-year agreement

excerpt.rendered: Double British Touring Car Champion Tom Ingram will remain part...

content.rendered:
Double British Touring Car Champion Tom Ingram will remain part of the Team VERTU line-up for at least the next three seasons of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship after agreeing a new extended deal that will run until the end of the 2029 season.

Ingram joined forces with the EXCELR8-run team ahead of the 2021 campaign and has cemented his position amongst the most successful drivers in series history over the course of the last six seasons.

Having secured a first win for the team at Snetterton in 2021, Ingram went on to finish fourth in the standings in his first year at the wheel of the Hyundai i30 Fastback N realising a life-long dream twelve months later when he became BTCC champion for the first time.

Following two seasons as runner-up, Ingram then reclaimed the title in 2025 during a season in which he also helped Team VERTU to secure the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ title.

Ingram’s extended deal comes on the back of EXCELR8 extending its title partnership agreement with award-winning automotive retailer Vertu, which was recently named as Automotive Retailer of the Year for the second successive year at the Autotrader Retailer Awards.

The 33-year-old - who has scored 29 wins and 84 podiums during his time with the team to date - will seek to join a select list of drivers to win three BTCC titles when the 2027 season gets underway at Donington Park in April.

Ingram will compete alongside the BTCC’s youngest ever full-time driver in the shape of Noah Young, with the other two members of the driver line-up to be confirmed in due course.

Tom Ingram, #80 Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “It goes without saying that I’m delighted to extend my deal with Team VERTU to at least the end of the 2029 season as this team feels like home and there is nowhere else I’d rather be.

“When I first signed with EXCELR8, this was a team that was still the new kid on the block with lofty ambitions of making it to the top, but I knew there was the chance to do something special.

“Over the last six seasons, we have shared so many highlights - from the first win at Snetterton through to twice lifting the title at Brands Hatch - and I’m hugely excited to see what we can achieve together over the next three seasons.

“Reclaiming the title next season is the obvious target, and everyone involved in the team is fully focused on making sure that we are in the best possible position to do that next season.”

Justina Williams, EXCELR8 Team Owner, said: “Tom’s record in the BTCC speaks for itself and we’re delighted to be able to confirm him as part of our driver line-up for at least three more seasons.

“From the moment he first got behind the wheel of the Hyundai, Tom has become a crucial part of the EXCELR8 story and his drive and desire to succeed has been reflected in the results we have secured together over the past six seasons.

“I have no doubt there will be plenty more silverware to come and we’re all working hard to challenge for title number three in 2027.”

title.rendered: Sutton stars as MN’s ‘Racer’s Racer of the Year’

excerpt.rendered: Motorsport News has conducted an exclusive poll of the top...

content.rendered:
Motorsport News has conducted an exclusive poll of the top ten finishers in the 2026 British Touring Car Championship to unearth the ‘Racer’s Racer of the Year’.

Unsurprisingly, record-breaking champion Ash Sutton topped the rankings from his peers in his NAPA UK Ford Focus Titanium, whilst the likes of Team VERTU’s Tom Ingram and CPRL’s Mercedes racer Adam Morgan also finished highly.

Others to feature in the top ten include Team VERTU Hyundai racer Nic Hamilton and Jack Sears Trophy winner Dexter Patterson in his Power Maxed Racing Audi A3, but to see the full rundown you’ll have to purchase this week’s Motorsport News.

Matt James, Motorsport News editor and BTCC reporter, said: “This is me dipping my responsibility to rate the drivers in print, but who better to ask than those strapped into the cockpit themselves? It is a really strong insight into the drivers who earn respect from their on-track rivals.

“Conducting this poll gives readers an insight into who the men on the grid think are those performing excellently. And the drivers themselves don’t generally tend to get things wrong.”

With Ash Sutton, Dan Cammish, Sam Osborne and newcomer Lewis Selby piloting the new Ford Focus Titanium, the Alliance Racing-run squad led the championship from the opening event. Team VERTU emerged as the closest challenger but couldn't eclipse the recent benchmark setters.

Here's how the Teams' Championship unfolded across ten events.

Donington Park

NAPA Racing UK made an immediate impact at Donington Park, with Sutton claiming two victories on the opening Sunday, including a one-two finish alongside Cammish in the second race.

The results gave NAPA Racing UK an early 33-point advantage over LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing (PMR), whose Audi squad enjoyed a strong start thanks to Mikey Doble's opening race victory and consistent results from Aiden Moffat.

WSR completed the top three, while Team VERTU endured a difficult opening event following Tom Ingram's exclusion from the first race.

The three pre-season events will provide a sustained build-up to the new campaign, with official BTCC activity beginning in early March and continuing towards the opening race weekend in April.

Further information regarding the Season Launch programme, spectator access and activities at each venue will be announced in due course.

The PM Junior Championship took another significant step towards its inaugural 2027 season with a successful Taster Day at Mallory Park, where 17 aspiring young drivers experienced the PM1 car first-hand.

Drivers from a range of backgrounds, including karting, sim racing and other junior motorsport categories, came together to try the car and discover what the new championship has to offer.

The morning sessions took place in predominantly dry conditions before rain arrived around lunchtime, leaving the circuit wet for the afternoon drivers.

The changing conditions did little to dampen the excitement. Feedback on the PM1 was consistently positive, offering further encouragement as preparations continue for the championship's first season.

Building the Next Generation

Developed by Power Maxed Racing, the PM Junior Championship offers a structured pathway for drivers aged 14–17, helping them progress from their early experiences in motorsport towards professional car racing.

At its heart is the PM1, a racing car designed to give young drivers a competitive platform to develop their skills, gain valuable experience and prepare for future opportunities in the sport.

Combining competitive racing with a strong emphasis on driver development, the championship brings together technical expertise, professional motorsport experience and opportunities for progression. It is built around three core pillars: Develop. Race. Progress.

Interest is also growing across the wider motorsport industry, with established organisations exploring the opportunities presented by the new series. This engagement highlights the PM Junior Championship's potential to become an important part of the pathway for future racing talent.

Looking Ahead to 2027

The Mallory Park Taster Day marks another milestone in the championship's preparations, giving prospective competitors a first-hand experience of the PM1 and a clearer understanding of the series ahead of its debut season.

As interest builds among drivers and the wider motorsport industry, Power Maxed Racing is working to establish a competitive, development-focused environment for the next generation of racing drivers.

The ambition goes beyond launching a new championship. By combining quality racing with opportunities to learn, develop and progress, the PM Junior Championship aims to help young competitors take the next steps in their motorsport careers.

Further details about the PM Junior Championship, driver opportunities and the 2027 season will be announced through the championship's official channels.

excerpt.rendered: Award-winning automotive retailer Vertu has extended its partnership with title-winning...

content.rendered:
Award-winning automotive retailer Vertu has extended its partnership with title-winning BTCC team EXCELR8 through to the end of the 2029 season, underlining its long-term commitment to one of the most successful teams in recent series history.

Vertu, which recently retained the title of Retailer of the Year at the Autotrader Retailer Awards, has worked with the Droitwich-based team since 2021, and took up the role of title sponsor twelve months later.

A stunning campaign saw the team secure the 2022 title thanks to Tom Ingram, and it then emerged on top in Britain’s premier racing series again in 2025.

Ingram lifted the Drivers' Championship for a second time, whilst Team VERTU completed a title treble by securing both the Teams' Championship and the Manufacturers'/Constructors' Championship.

Ahead of the 2027 season, the current agreement between Vertu and EXCELR8 has been further extended until at least the conclusion of the 2029 campaign, cementing the partnership as one of the longest-running and most successful commercial relationships in the BTCC paddock.

Team VERTU will continue to field a four-car programme in the BTCC next season and has already confirmed the signing of teenage racer Noah Young to compete alongside Ingram, who will be looking to reclaim the title having finished the 2026 season as runner-up.

The remaining two drivers in the line-up will be confirmed in due course ahead of the campaign getting underway at Donington Park in April.

Justina Williams, EXCELR8 Team Owner, said: "We’re hugely proud of the strength of our relationship with Vertu, and to be able to confirm an extension to cover the next three seasons in the BTCC.

"Vertu has played a major role in the success we've enjoyed in recent years, helping us build a championship-winning programme that has delivered race victories, multiple titles and consistent on-track success.

“The security of knowing we can count on Vertu’s support through to at least the end of 2029 allows us to focus on long-term planning, and we’re looking forward to challenging for more titles alongside Vertu in the years to come.”

Robert Forrester, Chief Executive of Vertu, said: “Our partnership with EXCELR8 has delivered outstanding results both on and off the track, and has been a platform for building awareness of the Vertu brand whilst also allowing us to engage with audiences throughout the UK

"Since first joining forces with the team, we have enjoyed championship success, significant increases in brand awareness and countless opportunities to showcase the strength of the Vertu brand to millions of motorsport followers.

"This partnership works so well because of the shared drive and desire to constantly improve in order to maintain the highest levels of performance and remain at the very top.

"Extending our commitment through to the end of 2029 will allow us to build on everything we have achieved together so far, and we look forward to challenging for more success in the seasons ahead."

Speedworks Corolla Racing brought the curtain down on the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship in impressive fashion at Brands Hatch, with two podium finishes for Josh Cook and another hugely encouraging weekend for Ryan Bensley.

Competing on the iconic Grand Prix circuit, the Cheshire-based outfit demonstrated the pace and potential of its Toyota Corolla GR Sport throughout the season finale, with Cook firmly amongst the frontrunners from the outset and Bensley continuing his rapid progression in Britain's premier domestic motorsport championship.

Sunday's opening encounter, Round 28 of the championship, delivered an impressive performance from Cook. Immediately involved in the battle for victory, the #66 demonstrated excellent racecraft on his way to second place.

Cook also recorded the fastest lap of the race, providing further evidence of the Corolla's outright competitiveness and securing another podium finish.

Further down the order, Bensley produced one of his most encouraging performances of the season to make up four places in the opening encounter.

Round 29 brought another opportunity for Cook to challenge at the front, and once again he delivered, securing his second runner-up finish of the afternoon and completing an impressive sequence of three consecutive top-three finishes across the Qualifying Race and Sunday's opening two encounters.

The final race of the season, Round 30, featured the traditional reverse-grid draw, with Cook selected to start eighth.

Running on the soft-compound tyre, Cook produced another measured and determined drive, working his way forward to sixth position at the chequered flag to complete a highly successful final weekend.

For Bensley, the championship finale provided a fitting conclusion to his first partial BTCC campaign. Producing another competitive drive and continuing to make progress through the field, he crossed the line in 14th position.

Josh Cook, #66, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "It was a really positive weekend and a great way to round off the championship. The car felt strong pretty much from the moment we rolled out, and that gave us the confidence to really attack.

"Qualifying was incredibly close. We topped our group and ultimately missed pole by just a couple of hundredths, which was frustrating, but it showed we had the pace to fight right at the front.

"The qualifying race was a good battle, and then on Sunday we were able to take another two podiums. Getting the fastest lap in Race One was particularly satisfying.

"Naturally, you always want to win, and when you're that close to the front you can't help feeling there was perhaps a little bit more available. But two second places, three podiums across the weekend and fourth in the championship was a strong way to finish.

"It was a season of highs and lows, and there were occasions where we had the speed without quite getting the reward. But the team never stopped pushing, and I can't thank everyone enough for the effort they've put in.

"There's a huge amount of potential in this package, and hopefully we've given everyone a good reminder of what we're capable of."

Ryan Bensley, #7, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "I absolutely loved that weekend. Brands Hatch GP is an incredible circuit, but it's also a massive challenge, particularly when you're still relatively new to touring cars.

"Qualifying wasn't quite where I wanted it to be, and that's definitely something I need to keep working on. It's about getting everything together over one lap, building confidence quickly and knowing exactly where the limits are.

"But the races were a completely different story. I felt like I was making progress every time I went out, and the pace we had, particularly on Sunday, was really encouraging.

"In Race One we went from 21st to 17th, and to be setting lap times comparable to cars much further up the field was a massive confidence boost. Then to finish the final race in 14th was a really positive way to end the year.

"I've learned an unbelievable amount since joining Speedworks. The level of engineering, preparation and support is incredible, and having someone like Josh alongside me has been invaluable.

"I know there's still a lot for me to learn, but I feel like I'm making some really big steps forward now. I'm already excited about what we can achieve in 2027, and I can't wait to keep building on everything we've learned this year."
